html:
Queen of Egypt and Great Royal Wife of the pharaoh Akhenaten, in the 1300s BCE. With her husband she led the worship of the sun disc Aten, the religion called Atenism.

She was unusually prominent for a queen. Reliefs show her the same size as the king, making offerings to the Aten, and even striking down enemies, a pose normally kept for pharaohs. The couple had six daughters and moved the court to a new city at Amarna.

What became of her is uncertain. An inscription shows she was still queen late in Akhenaten's reign, and some scholars think she ruled briefly as pharaoh after him under another name. Her tomb and mummy have never been surely identified. Tutankhamun, who restored the old gods, was probably her stepson.

She is famous today mostly through the painted Nefertiti Bust found at Amarna in 1912, now in Berlin.
